candidates.statement: 10. Must investigators who conduct studies outside of the United States sign a 1572? 53 [Revised 2021] 54
candidates.context: III. GENERAL QUESTIONS (10, 11, AND 13) 51 If a clinical study is conducted at a foreign site under an IND, all FDA IND regulations, 56 including the requirement to obtain a signed 1572 (21 CFR 312.53(c)(1)), must be met unless 57 the sponsor requests and is granted a waiver that provides for specific exceptions. In the case 58 where a foreign investigator cannot or will not sign Form FDA 1572 (e.g., because regional, 59 national, or local laws or regulations prohibit its signing), the sponsor may submit a request for 60 a waiver of the 1572 signature requirement under 21 CFR 312.10 (see section [IV] of this 61 guidance); alternatively, the site may operate as a non-IND site, in which case the study would 62 be conducted as a non-IND study. 63

candidates.statement: Investigators are responsible for complying with the applicable laws and regulations of the 75 country in which the study is being conducted, regardless of whether the study is being 76 conducted under an IND. We recommend that sponsors obtain signed, written statements from 77 investigators acknowledging their commitment to comply with regional, national, or local laws 78 and requirements. In addition, if a foreign clinical study is being conducted under an IND, the 79 investigator must sign Form FDA 1572 (investigator statement) (21 CFR 312.53(c)(1)) and 80 ensure that the study is conducted in accordance with the investigator statement and all other 81 applicable regulations under 21 CFR part 312 unless the sponsor has requested, and FDA has 82 granted, a waiver of the signature requirement. candidates.statement: 40. What should a sponsor submit to the IND when requesting a waiver of the 1572 signature 133 requirement? 134 [New 2021] 135
candidates.context: Under FDA regulations, sponsors may submit requests to FDA for a waiver of an IND 125 requirement (21 CFR 312.10). Such submissions may include request for a waiver of the 126 requirement that sponsors obtain an investigator signature on Form FDA 1572 (21 CFR 312.53 127 (c)(1)). Waiver of the signature on Form FDA 1572, when granted, enables the study at foreign 128 sites to be and/or remain under an IND even though the investigator at those foreign sites cannot 129 or will not sign Form FDA 1572, provided that the sponsor complies with the terms of the 130 waiver. (See below for further information regarding the waiver process and commitments.) 131 1. A clear statement that the sponsor is requesting a waiver of the signature requirement on 137 the 1572 138
